_comment: Program Management Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor. Structurally distinct from every other family plan: PM controls are organizational (not system-level) per NIST SP 800-53 r5 — they describe org-wide programs (Information Security Program Plan, Risk Management Strategy, Continuous Monitoring Strategy, etc.) rather than system-specific implementations. PM controls are NOT selected via LMH or privacy baselines — NIST treats them as always-required for organizations operating any federal information system, selected independently. This plan therefore documents how *this system* relates to and inherits from the *organization's* PM program. Most guided controls render with explicit inheritance posture (similar to PE / MA). Closes the 17-family Tier 1-4 plan rollout.
title: Program Management Plan
description:
Documents how the organizational Program Management framework — Information Security Program Plan, Privacy Program Plan, Risk Management Strategy, Continuous Monitoring Strategy, POA&M process, system inventory, enterprise architecture, mission / business-process definition, insider-threat program, workforce program, testing / training / monitoring program, threat-awareness program, supply-chain-risk strategy, data governance, and complaint management — applies to this system. Covers the controls of the PM family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-37 r2 (RMF), NIST SP 800-39 (Managing Information Security Risk), NIST SP 800-181 r1 (Workforce Framework), NIST IR 8062 (Privacy Risk Management Framework), and OMB Circular A-130 (Managing Information as a Strategic Resource).

Note: PM controls are organizational rather than system-specific — most controls in this plan are documented as inherited from the organization's PM program with system-specific extensions where applicable.
intro_template:
This Program Management Plan documents the relationship between {system_name} and the organizational Program Management framework. It establishes how this system relies on, contributes to, and inherits from the organization's Information Security Program Plan, Privacy Program Plan, Risk Management Strategy, Continuous Monitoring Strategy, POA&M process, enterprise architecture, and other org-level program elements.

The scope covers the system's relationship with each PM control in NIST SP 800-53 r5. Note: PM controls are organizational, not system-specific — most are documented here as inherited from the organization's PM program, with system-specific extensions where applicable. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Program Management family), NIST SP 800-37 r2 (Risk Management Framework), NIST SP 800-39 (Managing Information Security Risk), and OMB Circular A-130.
approach_template:
The {organization_name} information-security program is governed by {ispp_program_lead_role} per the Information Security Program Plan at {ispp_location}. The privacy program is governed by {privacy_program_lead_role} per the Privacy Program Plan at {privacy_program_plan_location}. The Risk Management Strategy is at {rms_location}; the Continuous Monitoring Strategy is at {conmon_strategy_location}. {system_name} is recorded in the system inventory at {system_inventory_location} as system identifier {system_inventory_id}; its POA&M items are tracked in {poam_system} under prefix {poam_id_prefix}.

Additional details on this system's relationship to each PM program area are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Program-management performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (system-inventory currency, POA&M-item closure rate, ConMon strategy adherence, ISPP review-cycle currency, mission-process alignment currency). The organizational PM program is reviewed on the cadence in §6.2 — typically annually with quarterly check-ins; this system surfaces to the org PM program as a tracked entity in the system inventory and a contributor to org-wide metrics. Org-level reports (POA&M roll-up, system inventory delta, threat-environment briefings) are received by the system's PM-2 program lead role on the cadence required by the organizational PM program.
integration_template: This Program Management Plan is the meta-frame for every other family plan in this RMF package. The CA family relies on PM-31 ConMon strategy as its umbrella; the RA family relies on PM-9 / PM-28 risk-management strategy; the SR family relies on PM-30 supply-chain-risk strategy; the AC / AU / IR / etc. families rely on PM-3 resources, PM-13 workforce, and PM-14 testing / training / monitoring. The PT family overlaps with PM-18 / PM-19 / PM-20 / PM-21 / PM-22 / PM-25 / PM-26 / PM-27 privacy program elements. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where PM-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables — though for PM, almost every other family plan inherits from PM rather than the reverse.

glossary.definition: Continuous Monitoring — CA-7 is the system-level Continuous Monitoring control; PM-31 is the org-level Continuous Monitoring Strategy. Most plans inherit from PM-31 and supplement at CA-7.
Per PM-23, an organizational body that governs data-related policy, standards, and quality. Distinct from the DIB which is privacy-specific.
Per PM-24 and Privacy Act § (u), federal-agency board responsible for oversight of computer-matching agreements.
Per PM-7, the organization's framework documenting business capabilities, processes, data, applications, and infrastructure. Federal common frameworks: FEAF, DoDAF.
Federal Enterprise Architecture Framework — common federal EA framework. Reference OMB guidance.
Per PM-1, the organizational plan documenting the information-security program. Reference NIST SP 800-37 r2 § 1.4.
In RMF, the practice where a control's implementation is provided by an underlying entity (organization, hosting provider). PM controls are almost universally inherited from the organization.
Mission Essential Function — per CNSSI 4009, a function whose loss would result in unacceptable mission impact. Mapped via PM-11 / RA-9.
NIST SP 800-181 r1 — National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education Workforce Framework. Per PM-13.
Managing Information as a Strategic Resource — federal guidance establishing the umbrella policies for federal information management. Drives many PM controls.
The Program Management family of NIST SP 800-53 r5 — controls that are organizational rather than system-specific. Not selected via LMH baselines; always required where applicable.
Plan of Action and Milestones — the recordkeeping for known security weaknesses with remediation plans. Per PM-4 (org-level) and CA-5 (system-level).
Per PM-18, the organizational plan documenting the privacy program. Often distinct from the ISPP. Reference NIST IR 8062.
Per NIST SP 800-39 / PM-28, the establishment of risk-management context: assumptions, constraints, risk tolerance, and priorities.
Per PM-9, the organizational strategy describing how risk is identified, assessed, responded to, and monitored across the org. Reference NIST SP 800-39 § 3.1.
Per PM-5, the organizational record of all systems / information-systems within scope. Federal: FISMA inventory + agency CMDB.
Per PM-16, the organizational program for tracking and disseminating threat intelligence. Often paired with TIP and SI-5.
